description: USE THIS when someone asks whether a car, SUV, van, truck or high-clearance rig can get to a named national forest camp, or which road leads there and when it is listed. It returns the Forest Service Motor Vehicle Use Map record of the road nearest the camp pin: road number and name, the vehicle classes the record lists (passenger vehicles, high-clearance vehicles), the recorded dates, the maintenance level, the surface as recorded and the distance from the road to the camp, set against the rig class you give. The record has no SUV, van or truck class, so those are shown against both classes. Optional date (YYYY-MM-DD) says whether that day falls inside or outside the recorded dates. It is the record, not today's condition, and says so: it knows nothing of washouts, closures, gates, weather or the last stretch to the pin, and it never says a rig can make it. Covered: camps in 20 national forests (the answer's `coverage` says which). BLM roads, other forests and a forest the Forest Service layer carries no roads for answer 'unrecorded' plus the office to ask; do not guess. Answers include `say` (two sentences to speak) and `tiny` (under 160 characters for a satellite text).

camp.description: A camp record id from find_camps (best) or the camp's name.

date.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD to compare with the road's recorded dates. Default: today (UTC).

rig.description: The rig class to compare with the record's vehicle classes.

name: road_to_camp
title: The recorded road to a camp, against your rig
